name: Korinek et al. 2026, faithful port (paper equations), Substantial scenario
description:
A port of the model in Korinek, Jones, Sacher, Cotter & McCrory (2026), "Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI" (Anthropic Institute WP 2026-02), written from the paper's own equations: Table A.1 (the 44 monthly equations of panels A-D and the steady state of panel E), Proposition 1 (eqs 14-18), the labour-market block (eqs 27-39) and the ideas block (eqs 22, 42), at the Table 1 calibration. Monthly from 2024.0 (t0) to 2030.0, the date the paper's scenario values and Table 3 refer to.

Structure: exogenous scenario paths m_t, d_t (logistics through the mid-2026 anchors, eq 8/8prime) and a_t (linear); the full-employment economy of Proposition 1 gives the targets; two occupation groups (cognitive C, all other N) move toward them through quits, layoffs at a sticky cognitive wage, openings, and a den Haan-Ramey-Watson matching function with a cross-group search discount; the reported economy is system (39) at realised employment; research rises with the GDP gap and feeds the ideas stock.

Base file = the SUBSTANTIAL scenario. overlays/korinek-faithful-modest.json and -extreme.json set the other two scenarios' Table 1 values; -pegged-rental.json (epsilon = infinity, Table 5) and -rigid-wage.json (xi = 0.9, Table 6) are sensitivity overlays. Tests reproduce every Table 3 row for the base; the overlays carry the other columns.

Authoring workarounds, none of which changes the mathematics: the four capital-market roots are solved for the capital share rather than the rental gap so every log stays finite; epsilon enters as invEps = 1/epsilon so a pegged rental rate is invEps = 0; the unemployment pools are stocks of their deviation from the steady state (so a stock never starts from a solve result); the lagged finding rate enters as f/f-bar with history 1. Where the paper leaves a step implicit the reading follows the authors' explorer code, which was run as an oracle and not copied; see docs/design/research/korinek-2026-model.md.
scope: US, 2024-2030, one country, two occupation groups, no policy: what GDP, factor prices, the labour share, employment and unemployment do along an assumed AI capability, diffusion and productivity path. The AI paths are inputs chosen by scenario, not predictions, and the model says nothing about which scenario is likely. It is the authors' structural model at their calibration, so its numbers inherit their assumptions (task CES with sigma = 0.5, uniform parameters across affected tasks, capital supplied along Delta ln K = epsilon Delta ln r, a lab-equipment ideas sector, search frictions calibrated to 2010-19 CPS flows). It reproduces the paper's Table 3, 5 and 6; that shows the port is faithful, not that the scenarios are right. Beyond 2030 or far outside the published parameter ranges it is the same model extrapolated, with no additional backing.
license: Model file CC0. The model, equations and calibration are those of Korinek, Jones, Sacher, Cotter & McCrory (2026).

solves.residual: log(kPot / Bt) / (1 - sigma) - invEps * (log(kPot / sK) + (sigma * log((1 - kPot) / sL) + lNtilde) / (1 - sigma) + dlnA - log(kPot / Bt) / (1 - sigma))
solves.description: Proposition 1, eq (18): epsilon Delta ln r = Delta ln K with Delta ln K from eq (17), written as Delta ln r - (1/epsilon) Delta ln K = 0. Unknown reparametrised to the capital share k = 1 - s_L,t = B_t e^{(1-sigma) Delta ln r} (eq 14), so every log in the residual is finite on the whole open unit interval; the bracket is that interval (structural), not a chosen bound. Strictly monotone (eq 18); at invEps = 0 the root is Delta ln r = 0.

solves.residual: (HBarC / (poolShareC * Ubar + muBar * (1 - poolShareC) * Ubar) + muBar * HBarN / (muBar * poolShareC * Ubar + (1 - poolShareC) * Ubar)) * poolShareC * Ubar - HBarC
solves.description: Steady state eq (38): U-bar_C = e U-bar splits the pool so that f-bar_C U-bar_C = H-bar_C, at mu-bar. The N condition then holds by the hires identity (37). Solved at every step but depends only on parameters, so it is the t0 steady state.

solves.residual: wC * (hirePerSearchMax / chiScaledInv) * pow(1 - pow(hirePerSearchC * chiScaledInv / hirePerSearchMax, iota), 1 / iota) + (1 - wC) * (hirePerSearchMax / chiScaledInv) * pow(1 - pow(hirePerSearchN * chiScaledInv / hirePerSearchMax, iota), 1 / iota) - piBarMean
